purpose: Bind manuscript claims to the framework behaviour that realizes them, so the two cannot drift apart silently. Every check is BEHAVIOURAL - it executes the framework and observes what it does - because a grep for a guard cannot distinguish live code from a comment or a dead branch.

verdicts.CONSISTENT: The framework was executed and behaved as the paper claim requires.
verdicts.DIVERGENT: The framework does not do what the paper says. Blocks publication of that claim.
verdicts.CANNOT_CHECK: The binding could not be evaluated. Explicitly NOT 'checked and fine'.
verdicts.accepted_divergence: A DIVERGENT binding whose resolution has been decided and recorded. The verdict stays DIVERGENT - acceptance never makes the code consistent, it only records that a human chose the repair. Requires a closure_action, so it cannot silence a finding without saying what will be done.

bindings.claim_text: Unrestricted open-world completeness is not finitely certifiable, so the software has no ABSOLUTELY_COMPLETE success state and can report only BOUNDED_CLOSED relative to a declared search world.
bindings.framework_obligation: No saturation run may ever report absolute completeness, however many conditions are satisfied.
bindings.check_note: Constructs a maximally-satisfied saturation run - five fully-flat, fully-audited rounds with a distant freshness cutoff - and asserts absolute_complete is still False. The schema pin alone would not catch a code path that bypassed it.

bindings.claim_text: If a bounded-saturated state is followed by a round with non-zero marginal epistemic growth, the state is no longer saturated until the required number of subsequent flat rounds is observed again.
bindings.framework_obligation: Appending one substantive-growth round to a saturated sequence must drop the verdict out of BOUNDED_SATURATED.
bindings.check_note: Two-part probe with its own control: first establish that an all-flat sequence DOES saturate (otherwise the reopening test is vacuous and returns CANNOT_CHECK), then append one growth round and require the verdict to change.

bindings.claim_text: No real-valued score can faithfully represent a partial order containing incomparable elements; a scalar can be a policy projection but cannot preserve the epistemic structure.
bindings.framework_obligation: Comparison surfaces must refuse to emit an aggregate score. This is the machine-checked theorem RaklFormal.no_faithful_scalarization applied to the shipped comparison machinery.
bindings.check_note: Schema pin plus inspection of the audit dataclass surface for any score/rank/composite field. Ties Paper I's order-theoretic result to issue #588's no-ORION_SCORE rule.

bindings.claim_text: A comparison that confounds model, tool access, hidden retrieval corpus, evaluator or budget is a system-level observation and never licenses an architecture-level claim.
bindings.framework_obligation: No proprietary system may be marked eligible for a causal architecture arm.
bindings.check_note: Executes the eligibility function over the live registry and cross-references availability. Guards the exact error issue #588 forbids: writing 'ORION architecture > System X architecture' from a confounded comparison.

bindings.claim_text: The companion gate assured_materialize_validated_quotient 'is a dormant sidecar with no production caller'; 'wiring this gate into the call graph is registered open work'.
bindings.framework_obligation: A symbol whose docstring declares it a production path must be reachable from something other than a test.
bindings.check_note: Scans src/rakl for docstrings whose FIRST LINE begins 'Production', then requires a non-test referrer. Deliberately narrow: matching any mention of 'production' fires on six further symbols that merely discuss it, and a checker that cries wolf on its first real run gets switched off.

accepted_divergence.finding: BOTH SIDES MISDESCRIBE. (a) The paper is STALE: it says the gate has no production caller and that wiring is open work, but src/rakl/semantic_quotient_runtime.py:107 is exactly that wiring layer and calls the gate at 132-134. (b) The CODE OVERSTATES: its docstring calls itself the 'Production quotient-consumption path', yet its only referrers are tests/test_integration_epoch_wiring.py and tests/test_semantic_quotient_runtime.py. TypedShortcutResolutionV3 has the same defect. The paper's CONCLUSION survives - premise (iii) is still not machine-enforced on a live path - but its stated REASON is wrong.
accepted_divergence.closure_action: Operator decision, two independent repairs. CODE: soften both docstrings to describe a gated entry point consumers must use, not one that is currently used - or wire a real caller. PAPER: replace 'dormant sidecar with no production caller / wiring is registered open work' with the accurate reason - a wiring layer exists but its call chain terminates in tests, so the premise is still not enforced on a live path. Not done unilaterally: this edits a premise-discharge claim in a manuscript that concurrent sessions are actively editing.

open_residuals.statement: Only 4 bindings exist, covering Papers I and VI. Papers II, III, IV and V have no claim-to-framework bindings yet.
open_residuals.closure_action: Add bindings per paper as each paper's load-bearing claims are settled. Coverage is not completeness: an unbound claim is unchecked, not consistent.

open_residuals.statement: Bindings are hand-authored, so a paper claim with no binding is invisible to this checker rather than reported as unbound.
open_residuals.closure_action: Cross-reference the Paper I theorem inventory so every theorem-like claim is either bound, or explicitly recorded as not-framework-bearing.

open_residuals.statement: PFC-PRODUCTION-PATH-IS-LIVE is DIVERGENT on two symbols and is accepted pending an operator decision on both the code docstrings and the Paper V sentence.
open_residuals.closure_action: Apply both repairs in accepted_divergence.closure_action, then remove the acceptance so the binding must go CONSISTENT.
